title: VPC deployment: connectivity hardening profiles and validation checklist
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Purpose: Define a concise set of connectivity-hardening profiles and an automated validation checklist for Private/VPC deployments. These profiles capture common customer constraints for regulated and air-gapped environments (e.g., no outbound egress, strict proxy-only bootstrap, ephemeral mirror usage) and the corresponding acceptance gates for upgrades, bootstrap, and runtime operations.

Why: We continue to see variability in customer networking policies that cause manual cut-and-paste runbooks and brittle upgrades. A small set of hardened profiles + machine-checkable validation will reduce upgrade rollbacks, decrease SRE touch time, and shorten onboarding for enterprise customers.

Scope:
- In scope: Define 3 production profiles (Minimal-Egress, Proxy-Only, Sealed-Airgap) with explicit network contracts. Produce checklist items for preflight, canary upgrade simulation, operator rollout, and rollback validation. Provide integration tests and example manifests.
- Out of scope: Rewriting operator code; implementing new cryptographic primitives (we will rely on existing image signing/KMS components).

Deliverables: profile spec document, preflight validator scripts (bash + k8s probes), a CI job for upgrade-sim tests, acceptance criteria list, runbook snippets for customers and support, and updated onboarding doc in Confluence.
acceptance_criteria: Profile definitions: Three distinct profiles (Minimal-Egress, Proxy-Only, Sealed-Airgap) exist as YAML schemas with clear required/optional fields and documented assumptions.

Deterministic bootstrap: For Sealed-Airgap profile, a documented artifact-mirroring procedure plus a signed artifact checksum verification step must allow a fresh cluster bootstrap with zero outbound egress to public networks.
Preflight validator: A CLI/helm preflight check returns explicit PASS/WARN/FAIL codes and produces a machine-readable report used by the operator to block or allow upgrade flows.

Upgrade canary: Canary upgrade simulation can be executed in CI that replays customer-like network constraints (simulate latency, blocked endpoints, proxy auth) and reports observable regressions (control-plane API errors, image fetch failures, KMS rotation failures).
Rollback verification: Automated rollback step validates that KV cache integrity and model artifacts remain consistent after rollback and that no key material was left in transient storage.

Telemetry fallback: In Sealed-Airgap and Proxy-Only modes, telemetry toggles to local aggregation and preserves minimal logs required for post-upgrade diagnostics; the absence of cloud telemetry must not block upgrade completion.

Operator upgrade contract: Operator will not require external DNS queries during upgrade in Proxy-Only and Sealed-Airgap if mirrored endpoints are configured; tests must pass with DNS stubbed to local host.

KMS rotation test: A simulated KMS rotation during upgrade completes successfully using customer-provided KMS endpoints or local HSM abstraction; documented manual steps exist if automated rotation cannot be used.
Documentation & runbooks: All profiles include a short customer-facing checklist (preflight commands, required mirror URLs, proxy config examples) and an SRE runbook for diagnosing failures.
Security review: Security sign-off recorded in ticket and security checklist items marked as mitigated or accepted.

CLI/Console UX: Console surfaces profile selection during onboarding and shows preflight report with linkable failure items (no UX blocking required for this PRD, but acceptance includes a stub UI flag).
rollout_plan: Phased rollout: (1) publish profile spec and preflight validator as alpha; (2) run internal canary on staging with two existing enterprise customers; (3) extend CI to run upgrade-sim tests nightly; (4) enable GA for new Private deployments and provide a migration guide for existing customers. Each phase gated by acceptance criteria above and a retro after internal canary.
success_metrics: Reduction in upgrade-related SEV escalations for private customers by 60% in first quarter after GA
Time-to-onboard (first successful bootstrap) reduced from average 6 days to 2 days for customers using a hardened profile
Preflight validator adoption: 80% of new private deployments run preflight before first upgrade
Automated rollback success rate >= 95% in simulated canary runs
risks_mitigations: Risk: Customers have bespoke network middleboxes that break mirrored bootstrap. Mitigation: provide a diagnostic mode and detailed connectivity logs plus a recommended support escalation path.
Risk: Edge cases for proprietary KMS implementations. Mitigation: ship manual KMS rotation runbook and test harness; mark as unsupported only when hardware constraints prevent safe rotation.
Risk: Telemetry blackout impedes debugging. Mitigation: require minimal local metrics collection and a configurable secure out-of-band artifact bundle the customer can upload for diagnostics.
Risk: Validator false negatives/positives. Mitigation: include WARN state and human-in-the-loop override; iterate validator rule set after initial pilots.
